correctness.rationale: The divisor weights follow from sigma(2^i p^j), the complete-sequence lemma is necessary and sufficient, and all exclusions have explicit minimal uncovered integers. Five finite base lists pass the exact greedy criterion. An analytic row/column extension lemma reduces infinitely many additions to two margins. All four axis-increment formulas are derived and positive on p=3,a>=2,b>=1 or p=5,a>=3,b>=1; seed margins are (141,77),(106,141),(37,106),(551,206),(302,551). The attached standalone checker verifies 90 direct divisor weights, 720 finite rectangles and 400 margin identities, but this finite evidence is not treated as an infinite proof. Scope p odd prime, a,b positive is explicit; limitations outside support {2,p} remain.

originality.rationale: The original source Schwab–Thompson, arXiv:1701.08504, §6, proves infinitude and zero density of s-practicals, not an exact two-prime-support characterization. Aidun–Thompson arXiv:2604.05284 has distribution and moment theorems for S_s, not this subset-sum classification. OEIS A393492 is an initial finite table (including the five minimal bases), which does not imply infinite necessity and sufficiency. The closest exact published two-prime-support findings use ordinary divisor weights or Carmichael weights, not s(d). A relevant 2026 Utrecht thesis is inaccessible and remains an explicit risk, not treated as inspected whole-document noncoverage.
residual_risks: The full text of Reuijl’s 2026 thesis is inaccessible; possible theorem overlap cannot be excluded from available evidence.

value.rationale: s-practical numbers have a current sequence enumeration and a newly studied nonmultiplicative divisor-sum aggregate. An exact natural two-prime-support classification and five minimal exponent generators give a structural explanation for composite examples and forbid all p>=7, beyond finite sequence extension. The positive quadrants generate infinite examples, with explicit closure inequalities that can inform related nonmultiplicative practical-number investigations.
